signals.problem: SDAIA has moved into active PDPL enforcement: 48 committee decisions against organizations in roughly the past year, fines up to SAR 5 million per violation (doubling for repeat offenses), and criminal liability (up to 2 years prison, fines up to SAR 3 million) for intentional misuse of sensitive data. Common violations are lack of legal basis for processing, no consent for marketing, and missing technical/organizational safeguards — exactly the gaps typical SMEs and startups have.
signals.customer: Saudi SMEs, e-commerce stores and startups handling customer personal data who have no dedicated legal/compliance function
signals.source: Web search: IAPP, law-firm compliance blogs, SDAIA-related coverage

evidence.summary: Law firm blog summarizing SDAIA's enforcement statistics and the most common compliance failures (no legal basis, no consent for marketing, missing safeguards); seen via search snippet.

evidence.claim: Saudi's data protection authority has stepped up enforcement activity

signals.problem: Between Nov 2025 and Apr 2026 MHRSD launched a new 3-year Nitaqat cycle with profession-level Saudization quotas across 269 roles (e.g., engineering 30%, accounting 40%→70% over 5 years, marketing/sales 60%, 69 admin roles 100%, procurement 70%), raised minimum Saudi wage thresholds to count toward quota (SAR 4,000 general, up to SAR 8,000-9,000 for specific professions), and eliminated the Yellow tier — making the system far more granular and harder for SME employers to track manually.
signals.customer: SME employers (5+ employees in a given profession) across engineering, accounting, marketing, admin and procurement functions who must track evolving profession-specific quotas

signals.problem: The Saudi E-Commerce Law requires anyone selling online — including via a plain website, app, or social-media account — to register a commercial registration and obtain Maroof certification from the Ministry of Commerce, disclose full pre-purchase information, honor a 7-day return right, localize customer personal data storage, and integrate ZATCA e-invoicing once above the VAT threshold. This formalizes a huge previously-informal population of Instagram/Snapchat/WhatsApp sellers.

signals.source: Web search: Saudipedia, origami.sa, Ministry of Commerce Maroof coverage

evidence.summary: Compliance-guide article explicitly stating social-media sellers fall under the law and must register on Maroof; seen via search snippet.
